group.passage:
Late in 2015, as Oxford marked 200 years since Ada Lovelace’s birth, a sequence of numbers was developed into a musical theme. The numbers came from a simulator of the Analytical Engine, a calculating machine that had been designed but never built. The choice was fitting: Lovelace herself had once imagined that such an engine might compose music.
The engine was the work of Charles Babbage, who began designing it in the mid-1830s. It was to receive its instructions on punched cards, similar to those used to guide the designs woven on Jacquard looms. In 1842, an Italian engineer, Luigi Menabrea, published the first account of the machine, in French. The scientist Charles Wheatstone then asked Lovelace to translate it into English, and it was Babbage who proposed that she include notes of her own. The translation was printed in 1843 under just her initials, yet her notes accounted for 41 of its 66 pages. Her final note, Note G, showed how the engine could work out the Bernoulli numbers; many people now regard its table as the first computer program.
For Babbage, the engine was chiefly a number machine. Lovelace looked further. The cards, she realized, set out operations, and those operations were independent of the data they were applied to. The engine was therefore not confined to arithmetic: in principle, whatever could be expressed through mathematical rules could be processed. If the relations among musical sounds in harmony could be put into such a form, she suggested, the engine might produce detailed compositions of any length or complexity.
Still, she refused to overstate the machine’s powers. In her view, it had no ability to originate anything; it could do only what people knew how to instruct it to do. When Alan Turing later took up this point, he named it “Lady Lovelace’s objection” and rejected it.
Her readiness to link numbers with art may owe something to her upbringing. Born in 1815 to the poet Lord Byron and his wife, Anne Isabella, she was taught mathematics and science at her mother’s wish, partly to keep her away from her father’s poetic side. If the goal was to remove every trace of the poet, it did not fully succeed: she described her own approach as “poetical science.” She died in 1852, at only 36, yet the theme from Oxford suggests that her imagination has lasted far longer.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true of the translation printed in 1843?

options.A: It was the first account of the engine to appear in print.
options.B: It was translated because Babbage asked Lovelace to do so.
options.C: Her added notes took up more than half of its pages.
options.D: It reported results that the engine itself had already produced.

questions.stem: Why did Lovelace believe that the engine might be able to handle music?

options.A: The instructions it followed were separate from the things it worked on.
options.B: Its cards had been taken from looms that wove patterns into cloth.
options.C: Babbage had designed it mainly to handle sounds rather than numbers.
options.D: Composers of her day already wrote their music in the form of numbers.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes Lovelace’s attitude toward what the engine could do?

options.A: She believed that it would one day be able to think for itself.
options.B: She was interested mainly in how well it could do arithmetic.
options.C: She doubted that anyone would ever manage to build it.
options.D: She saw wide possibilities in it but was honest about its limits.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes how the passage is organized?

options.A: Her life is told in time order, from her birth to her death.
options.B: A modern event leads into the history and ideas behind it.
options.C: Her view is set against Turing’s, and his is shown to be right.
options.D: Several inventors are compared to decide who built the first computer.

1.explanation_zh: 第二段說這篇譯文在 1843 年刊出時，全文 66 頁中她的注解就占了 41 頁。66 頁的一半是 33 頁，41 頁超過一半，所以「她加上的注解占了超過一半的篇幅」正確。這題要把文中的頁數換算成「超過一半」才看得出正解。
evidence: The translation was printed in 1843 under just her initials, yet her notes accounted for 41 of its 66 pages.

option_notes_zh.A: 細節錯置：第一篇介紹這台機器的文章，是梅納布雷亞 1842 年用法文發表的那篇；1843 年刊出的是它的英譯本（加上她的注解），不是第一篇。
option_notes_zh.B: 細節錯置（人物對調）：請她翻譯的是科學家惠斯登；巴貝奇提議的是請她「加上自己的注解」，不是請她翻譯。
option_notes_zh.D: 與原文相反：分析機從未建造出來（第一段），Note G 只是說明這台機器「可以如何」算出白努利數，不可能報告機器實際算出的結果。

A: In 1842, an Italian engineer, Luigi Menabrea, published the first account of the machine, in French.
B: The scientist Charles Wheatstone then asked Lovelace to translate it into English, and it was Babbage who proposed that she include notes of her own.
D: The numbers came from a simulator of the Analytical Engine, a calculating machine that had been designed but never built.
Her final note, Note G, showed how the engine could work out the Bernoulli numbers; many people now regard its table as the first computer program.

1.strategy_zh: 「下列何者正確」的細節題，每個選項都要回原文核對主詞、時間與數字。A 把 the first account 從 1842 年的法文原文搬到 1843 年的譯本；B 把 Wheatstone 換成 Babbage；D 要和第一段 never built 對照。有數字的句子常要換算：41／66 超過一半。
hints: 1843 年的譯文是第一篇介紹分析機的文章嗎？第一篇是哪一年、用什麼語言發表的？
請她翻譯的是誰？巴貝奇提議的又是什麼？
41 頁占 66 頁的比例有沒有超過一半？

2.explanation_zh: 第三段說她發現卡片設定的是「運算」，而這些運算和它們所作用的資料彼此獨立；therefore（因此）機器並不局限於算術，凡是能用數學規則表達的東西原則上都能處理，接著才推到「如果樂音之間的關係能轉成這種形式，機器就可能作曲」。也就是說，機器「接受的指令」和「處理的對象」是分開的，正是她認為機器能處理音樂的原因。
evidence: The cards, she realized, set out operations, and those operations were independent of the data they were applied to.
The engine was therefore not confined to arithmetic: in principle, whatever could be expressed through mathematical rules could be processed.

option_notes_zh.B: 細節錯置：第二段說分析機的打孔卡「類似」用來引導雅卡爾織布機織出圖案的卡片（similar to those），不是從織布機拿來的；而且這只是說明卡片的用法，不是她認為機器能作曲的理由。
option_notes_zh.C: 與原文相反：對巴貝奇來說，這台機器主要是處理數字的機器（chiefly a number machine），不是為了處理聲音而設計的。
option_notes_zh.D: 文中沒有提到當時的作曲家用數字寫音樂；她說的是「如果」樂音之間的關係能轉成數學形式，機器才可能作曲。

B: It was to receive its instructions on punched cards, similar to those used to guide the designs woven on Jacquard looms.
C: For Babbage, the engine was chiefly a number machine.
D: If the relations among musical sounds in harmony could be put into such a form, she suggested, the engine might produce detailed compositions of any length or complexity.

2.strategy_zh: 問「她為什麼認為可以」，要找因果連接詞：第三段的 therefore 前面那一句就是原因（運算和資料彼此獨立）。織布機那一句只是類比卡片的用法，而且是 similar to（類似），不是「來自」。
hints: 第三段 therefore 前面那一句說她發現了什麼？
卡片設定的「運算」和它處理的「資料」是什麼關係？
織布機那一句說的是卡片「類似」織布機的卡片，還是「來自」織布機？

3.explanation_zh: 第三段她認為機器原則上能處理任何能用數學規則表達的東西，甚至可能創作任何長度、任何複雜程度的樂曲——看見很大的可能性；第四段用 Still 轉折，說她不肯誇大機器的能力，強調機器不能自行創造，只能做人們知道如何指示它做的事——清楚它的限制。兩段合起來就是「看見廣大的可能，也坦白承認它的限制」。
evidence: If the relations among musical sounds in harmony could be put into such a form, she suggested, the engine might produce detailed compositions of any length or complexity.
Still, she refused to overstate the machine’s powers.
In her view, it had no ability to originate anything; it could do only what people knew how to instruct it to do.

option_notes_zh.A: 與原文相反：她認為機器 had no ability to originate anything，只能照人的指示做事，不可能「自己思考」。
option_notes_zh.B: 細節錯置（人物對調）：主要把它看成處理數字的機器的是巴貝奇；勒芙蕾絲 looked further，看到數字以外的用途。
option_notes_zh.C: 文中沒有說她懷疑有沒有人造得出這台機器；機器最後沒有建成是事實，但文中談的是她對機器「能做什麼」的看法。

A: In her view, it had no ability to originate anything; it could do only what people knew how to instruct it to do.
B: For Babbage, the engine was chiefly a number machine.
C: The numbers came from a simulator of the Analytical Engine, a calculating machine that had been designed but never built.

3.strategy_zh: 態度題要把同一個人在不同段落的說法合起來：第三段的「可能」（might produce）和第四段的「限制」（refused to overstate）缺一不可。只抓住「機器能作曲」就以為她認為機器有創造力，正好落入 A 的陷阱；B 則是把巴貝奇的看法安到她身上。
hints: 第三段她認為機器原則上能處理哪些東西？
第四段開頭的 Still 之後，她對機器的能力說了什麼？
哪個選項同時涵蓋「可能性」和「限制」？

4.explanation_zh: 第一段從 2015 年底牛津的音樂主題（一件現代的事件）開始；第二段回到 1830、1840 年代，交代分析機、她的譯文與注解；第三、四段說明她對機器作曲的構想與她指出的限制；第五段再談她的成長背景，最後回到牛津的音樂主題作結。整篇是「由一件現代的事件，帶出它背後的歷史與想法」。
evidence: Late in 2015, as Oxford marked 200 years since Ada Lovelace’s birth, a sequence of numbers was developed into a musical theme.
The choice was fitting: Lovelace herself had once imagined that such an engine might compose music.
The engine was the work of Charles Babbage, who began designing it in the mid-1830s.

option_notes_zh.A: 以偏概全：只有最後一段依序提到她的出生與去世；全文從 2015 年開始，再跳回 1830 年代，並不是依時間順序敘述她的一生。
option_notes_zh.C: 細節錯置：文中只說圖靈後來反駁了她的看法，並沒有判定誰對；圖靈也只在第四段出現一次。
option_notes_zh.D: 文中沒有比較多位發明家，也沒有說誰造出了第一台電腦；分析機從未建造，Note G 的表格只是「許多人視為第一個電腦程式」。

A: Late in 2015, as Oxford marked 200 years since Ada Lovelace’s birth, a sequence of numbers was developed into a musical theme.
Born in 1815 to the poet Lord Byron and his wife, Anne Isabella, she was taught mathematics and science at her mother’s wish, partly to keep her away from her father’s poetic side.
C: When Alan Turing later took up this point, he named it “Lady Lovelace’s objection” and rejected it.
D: The numbers came from a simulator of the Analytical Engine, a calculating machine that had been designed but never built.
Her final note, Note G, showed how the engine could work out the Bernoulli numbers; many people now regard its table as the first computer program.

4.strategy_zh: 結構題先標出每段的時間與功能：¶1 2015 年、¶2 1830 年代到 1843 年、¶3–4 她的想法與限制、¶5 成長背景並回到牛津。正解要符合「整篇」的安排；只符合一段的描述（例如最後一段從出生寫到去世）不能選。
hints: 第一段說的是哪一年的事？第二段又跳回哪個年代？
她的出生到第五段才提到，這樣的安排是依時間順序嗎？
文中有沒有判定圖靈和勒芙蕾絲誰對？

translation_zh.text:
2015 年底，牛津紀念愛達‧勒芙蕾絲誕生 200 週年之際，有一串數字被發展成一段音樂主題。這些數字來自「分析機」的模擬器；分析機是一台設計好了、卻從未建造出來的計算機器。選用這台機器再恰當不過：勒芙蕾絲本人當年就曾想像，這樣的機器也許能夠作曲。
這台機器出自查爾斯‧巴貝奇之手，他從 1830 年代中期開始設計它。它要透過打孔卡接收指令，類似用來引導雅卡爾織布機織出花樣的那種卡片。1842 年，一位義大利工程師路易吉‧梅納布雷亞用法文發表了第一篇介紹這台機器的文章。科學家查爾斯‧惠斯登隨後請勒芙蕾絲把它譯成英文，而提議她加上自己的注解的，則是巴貝奇。這篇譯文在 1843 年刊出時只署了她的姓名縮寫，但在全文 66 頁中，她的注解就占了 41 頁。她的最後一則注解 Note G 說明了這台機器可以如何算出白努利數；許多人如今把其中的表格視為第一個電腦程式。
對巴貝奇來說，這台機器主要是一台處理數字的機器。勒芙蕾絲看得更遠。她發現，卡片設定的是「運算」，而這些運算和它們所作用的資料是彼此獨立的。因此，這台機器並不局限於算術：原則上，凡是能用數學規則表達的東西都可以處理。她提出，如果和聲中各個樂音之間的關係能轉換成這樣的形式，這台機器就可能創作出任何長度、任何複雜程度的精細樂曲。
不過，她不肯誇大這台機器的能力。在她看來，它沒有能力自行創造任何東西；它只能做人們知道如何指示它去做的事。後來艾倫‧圖靈探討這個論點時，把它稱為「勒芙蕾絲夫人的反對意見」，並且加以反駁。
她之所以樂於把數字和藝術連在一起，或許和她的成長背景有關。她生於 1815 年，父親是詩人拜倫勳爵，母親是拜倫的妻子安妮‧伊莎貝拉；母親讓她學習數學與科學，部分原因是想讓她遠離父親那種詩人的性情。如果目的是抹去詩人留下的一切痕跡，那麼這個目的並沒有完全達成：她用「詩意的科學」來形容自己的思考方式。她在 1852 年去世，年僅 36 歲；然而牛津的那段音樂主題顯示，她的想像力留存得比她的生命長久得多。

open_tasks.prompt: In one English sentence, explain what Lovelace saw in Babbage’s engine that Babbage himself did not.
reference_answers: Lovelace saw that the engine could work on anything that follows mathematical rules, such as music, and not just on numbers.
Unlike Babbage, she realized that the machine could handle more than numbers, even music, as long as people told it how.
checklist_zh: 是不是一個完整的英文句子
有沒有點出「不只處理數字」
有沒有提到音樂或數學規則
有沒有和巴貝奇的看法做對比

open_tasks.prompt: Lovelace argued that a machine can only do what people know how to instruct it to do. Today some computer programs can write music. Do you think this proves her wrong? Answer in 1–2 English sentences and give one reason.
reference_answers: Not really, because a music program still follows the rules and examples that people have given it, so it is only doing what it was told to do.
I think it partly proves her wrong, because some programs now create tunes that even the people who made them could not have predicted.
checklist_zh: 有沒有清楚表明同意或不同意
有沒有連結到文中勒芙蕾絲或圖靈的觀點

D.explanation_zh: 與原文相反：分析機設計好了卻從未建造，不可能已經算出結果；Note G 說明的是機器「可以如何」算出白努利數（could work out），不是報告實際結果。

B.evidence: It was to receive its instructions on punched cards, similar to those used to guide the designs woven on Jacquard looms.
B.explanation_zh: 細節錯誤：文中說打孔卡「類似」雅卡爾織布機用的卡片（similar to those），不是從織布機拿來的；而且這句只說明機器如何接收指令，不是她認為機器能處理音樂的理由（理由是第三段 therefore 前那句：運算和資料彼此獨立）。

C.evidence: For Babbage, the engine was chiefly a number machine.
C.explanation_zh: 與原文相反：對巴貝奇來說，這台機器主要是處理數字的機器，不是為處理聲音而設計的。

D.evidence: If the relations among musical sounds in harmony could be put into such a form, she suggested, the engine might produce detailed compositions of any length or complexity.
D.explanation_zh: 文中沒有提到當時的作曲家用數字寫曲；她用 If 提出假設：「如果」樂音之間的關係能轉成數學形式，機器才可能作曲，可見這只是她的推想。

A.evidence: In her view, it had no ability to originate anything; it could do only what people knew how to instruct it to do.
A.explanation_zh: 與原文相反：她認為機器沒有能力自行創造任何東西，只能照人們知道如何下的指令去做，不可能「自己思考」。

B.evidence: For Babbage, the engine was chiefly a number machine. Lovelace looked further.
B.explanation_zh: 人物錯置：主要把機器看成處理數字工具的是巴貝奇；勒芙蕾絲 looked further，看到算術以外（例如音樂）的可能。

C.evidence: Still, she refused to overstate the machine’s powers.
C.explanation_zh: 文中談的是她對機器「能做什麼」的看法——看見廣大可能、但不誇大它的能力；完全沒有提到她懷疑有沒有人造得出來。機器最後沒有建成（第一段）是事實，不是她的態度。

A.evidence: Late in 2015, as Oxford marked 200 years since Ada Lovelace’s birth, a sequence of numbers was developed into a musical theme.
A.explanation_zh: 與原文的安排不符：全文從 2015 年的事件開始，再跳回 1830 年代；她的出生與成長到最後一段才提到，並不是依時間順序從出生寫到去世。

C.evidence: When Alan Turing later took up this point, he named it “Lady Lovelace’s objection” and rejected it.
C.explanation_zh: 文中只用一句說圖靈後來反駁她的論點，沒有判定誰對，更沒有用全文去證明圖靈是對的；這一句也不是全文的組織方式。

D.evidence: The numbers came from a simulator of the Analytical Engine, a calculating machine that had been designed but never built.
D.explanation_zh: 文中只有巴貝奇一位發明者，沒有比較多位發明家；分析機從未建成，文中也沒有討論誰造出了第一台電腦。

checked.claim: 題幹與選項中的事實性說法（第一篇介紹、誰請她翻譯、注解頁數、卡片與織布機、巴貝奇的看法、圖靈的反駁）

details.method_zh: 逐句比對選文、題幹與選項中的事實與數字和事實單 ada-lovelace-music-rt04（f1–f18）；四個來源（Bodleian s1–s4）於 2026-10-09 重新開啟逐條確認（見各條 note）。選文沒有事實單以外的具體細節（f4 De Morgan、f7 百年後才建成等未用到的事實不影響）。
